---
title: "01 · Beta–gamma channel and Laguerre modes"
description: "Turn a projected Gaussian distance into an exact scalar channel."
---

After reversible row orthonormalization, write

$$T=U+V,\qquad U\sim\chi_m^2,\quad V\sim\chi_{d-m}^2,$$

with `U` and `V` independent. The observed direction contains no additional
information about `T`, so recovery reduces to observing `U` from `T`.

```python
from rpgeom.ceilings import hgr_isotropic, laguerre_singvals, mutual_info
print(hgr_isotropic(64, 768))
print(laguerre_singvals(64, 768, kmax=5) ** 2)
print(mutual_info(64, 768))
```

The first Laguerre mode is the centered distance. Higher modes are progressively
harder: at fixed mode `k`, their recoverable variance is asymptotic to `(m/d)^k`.
